title: Can a data-based χ²/dof check detect a wrong wind?
question: Does the weighted-residual χ² per degree of freedom rise measurably when the estimator is told the wrong wind or when a source is omitted, at the sensor budgets of interest?
motivation: The identifiability flags depend only on the sensitivity matrix, so they cannot see a wrong model (known issue 2); hidden wind error is the dominant risk in the robustness runs.
method: Add χ²/dof to geodesign_robust rows on a copy (not the frozen results); compare matched, hidden-wind, unseen-wind and omitted-source conditions with the noise sd fixed from the validation scale.
expected: A separation between matched and mismatch conditions would justify a model-adequacy flag; no separation would mean wind error is invisible to these layouts.

title: How much of the ranking instability is discretisation rather than noise?
question: If truth and inference use the same finer mesh (or the upwind scheme), do small-budget layout rankings stabilise and do selected sites change?
motivation: Numerical diffusion dominates the nominal K (K_eff/K about 2.4–9.4 at the design mesh); the 250 m refinement used 3 fine design cases against 6 with no 500 m resampling baseline (known issue 4).
method: Repeat greedy selection at 500 m over resampled design subsets to get a baseline Jaccard, then compare with 250 m selections using matched case counts.
expected: If the 500 m resampling baseline already gives Jaccard 0–0.2, refinement instability is ordinary greedy instability.

title: What is the noise baseline of the ranking-stability metric?
question: With exactly-zero contrasts counted as 'kept' and no noise baseline, what fraction of rankings flips between two independent noise draws with no model change?
motivation: Known issue 3: the metric reads as 'rankings were never resolved', not as 'wind error flips them'.
method: Compute the same metric between two noise seeds under the matched condition and between matched and each mismatch; report zero-difference rows separately.
expected: A matched-vs-matched baseline close to the mismatch value would confirm rankings are unresolved at 6 test scenarios.

title: Does a wind-robust design objective change the chosen layouts?
question: Would greedy selection over an ensemble of perturbed winds (expected or worst case) give layouts that degrade less under a hidden wind error than matched-design layouts?
motivation: Matched-design layouts are not robust at 2–3 sensors under mismatch (F-017) and unknown wind error dominates the sensor-count effect (F-021).
method: Extend the design cases with perturbed-wind variants (perturb_wind / variant_case machinery exists), select greedily on the ensemble objective, evaluate on unseen winds with α frozen.
expected: Layouts selected under wind uncertainty may lose less on hidden-wind tests but some matched performance; the size of the trade-off is the result.

title: Replace the saturated weakly_constrained flag
question: Is there an identifiability diagnostic that varies across rows in the geodesign runs, e.g. with scales taken from a validation-ensemble prior width instead of 1e5 µg/s?
motivation: The flag fires on every geodesign row because the emission scale is small next to true emissions (known issue 2).
method: Recompute effective_rank and posterior std with scales set from validation-ensemble spreads (never test quantities) and check whether the flag now varies with layout and budget.
expected: A non-saturated flag that tracks actual error across layouts; if it still cannot detect model error, that supports the χ² check.
